Camila, hello. We have five minutes before the others join. How are things on your side?
Busy, in a good way. We closed the audit this week, so the team is lighter. How about you?
Travelling too much, honestly. I was in Milan on Monday and I am in Paris until Friday.
That sounds challenging with the time zones. Do you manage to keep your catch-ups with the regions?
Most of them. The Asia ones are hard. And your credit team, is the workload still high?
It is. One analyst is covering two portfolios, and that is my main concern this quarter.
Understood. Speaking of which, what would help most: a replacement or a temporary contract?
A replacement, because the volume is not temporary. By the way, are you coming to the offsite in November?
I am. Two days, and I would like to visit one of the entities while I am there.
Then let us touch base in October, so that I can organise the visit with the local team.

Camila, hi, good to see you. We have a few minutes before the others join, so tell me, how are things on your side? Things here have changed quite a lot, actually. My team was reorganised in April. Two business units became one, and now I cover both, which is interesting and also a lot. The time difference with you is five hours, and honestly that is the hardest part of my week, so I try to start these calls early in my afternoon. Anyway, I wanted to ask you something before the agenda. Would you like to have a short catch-up every two weeks? Thirty minutes, no agenda, just to hear what is happening in your region. I find that I learn more in those thirty minutes than in the monthly committee.

Let me show you the other version of the same five minutes. I open the call and I ask, how are things on your side? And the answer comes back: fine, thanks. That is all. So I try again. I ask, how is the new process working in your region? And the answer is: it is working well. Again, two seconds. After that we both look at the screen and wait for the others to join, and nobody learns anything. Nothing there was rude and nothing was wrong. The English was correct. But those five minutes before the agenda are where you find out what is really happening in another region, and where the other person finds out that they can call you when something is difficult. It is the cheapest thirty seconds of relationship you will ever buy.
